blocks.text: Feature Extraction, back in this same module, briefly covered pulling day of week, month, and a simple weekend flag out of a raw date column, useful, simple features that apply broadly across almost any dataset with a date. Date Features goes considerably deeper into that same raw material, covering techniques that address real, specific problems basic extraction leaves unresolved.

This topic covers the genuine problem with feeding raw month or day numbers directly into a model, the cyclical encoding technique that fixes it, time since a reference event as a genuinely powerful recency feature, incorporating real domain knowledge like holidays, extracting features from a full date and time value rather than just a date, and a genuine leakage trap specific to date features that connects directly back to the Data Leakage topic earlier in this course.
1. The Genuine Problem With Raw Month and Day Numbers

blocks.alt: The Genuine Problem With Raw Month and Day Numbers
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135306-200210975.png

Feeding a raw month number, 1 through 12, directly into most models creates a genuinely subtle but real problem, December, month 12, and January, month 1, are numerically about as far apart as two months can be, yet in genuine calendar time they sit right next to each other, December bleeding directly into January every single year.

A model treating month as a plain number has no genuine way to know this, it sees 12 and 1 as distant values, not adjacent ones, exactly the same problem applies to day of week, where Sunday and Monday are genuinely adjacent in real time but can end up numerically far apart depending on how they happen to be encoded.
2. Fixing It: Cyclical Encoding
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135306-659519189.png

Cyclical encoding solves this by genuinely wrapping the number line into a circle, using sine and cosine together to represent a date part, month, day of week, hour, as a position on that circle rather than a single, straight line number. December and January, mapped onto a circle, genuinely end up sitting close together, exactly matching their real calendar adjacency.

This technique produces two new columns, a sine component and a cosine component, replacing the single raw month or day number, and it is genuinely one of the more elegant, widely used tricks in practical feature engineering for exactly this cyclical class of problem.

blocks.text: 3. A Worked Example
Computing cyclical encoding for month with NumPy shows exactly how the sine and cosine transformation is genuinely applied in practice.

code.content:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "purchase_date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-12-28", "2026-01-03", "2026-06-15"]),
})

month = df["purchase_date"].dt.month
df["month_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * month / 12)
df["month_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * month / 12)

print(df)

blocks.text: December and January, months 12 and 1, now produce sine and cosine values that are genuinely close together, exactly resolving the numerical distance problem raw month numbers created.
4. Time Since a Reference Event
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135306-565097218.png

Computing the genuine number of days since a reference date, account creation, last purchase, last login, turns a single timestamp into a directly useful recency feature. This connects directly back to the days since last purchase example from the Domain Features topic, part of the broader RFM, recency, frequency, monetary value, pattern common in e-commerce and subscription businesses.

This technique is genuinely simple to compute but often carries real, strong predictive signal, a customer with a large number of days since their last purchase is often genuinely at higher risk of churning than one who purchased recently, exactly the kind of insight a raw purchase date column alone does not directly expose.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Recency features like days since last purchase are genuinely among the most reliable, broadly useful date derived features across many different real business problems, not just e-commerce.

blocks.text: 5. Incorporating Real Domain Knowledge: Holiday Flags

blocks.alt: Incorporating Real Domain Knowledge: Holiday Flags
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135307-26851922.png

Checking a raw date against a genuine, known calendar of holidays or special events produces an is holiday flag, a feature that pure date arithmetic alone could never generate on its own, since knowing which specific dates are holidays requires genuine external, domain specific knowledge, not just the date value itself.

This connects directly back to the Domain Features topic earlier in this module, a holiday flag is genuinely a domain feature, expertise about which dates matter for a specific business, expressed here specifically as a date derived feature rather than a purely numeric one.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Maintain a genuine, reusable holiday or event calendar for the specific business or region a project involves, rather than recomputing one manually every time. It becomes a genuinely reusable input across many different date feature projects.

blocks.text: 6. Extracting From a Full Date and Time Value

blocks.alt: Extracting From a Full Date and Time Value
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135307-826637658.png

When a column includes a genuine time component, not just a date, hour of day and an is business hours flag become available as additional, genuinely useful features. A support ticket submitted at 3 in the morning behaves very differently, and might warrant genuinely different treatment, than one submitted at 2 in the afternoon on a business day.

This extends the same underlying idea covered throughout this topic, a single timestamp genuinely contains far more extractable signal than it first appears to, once you know specifically what to pull out of it.

blocks.text: 7. A Genuine Leakage Trap Specific to Date Features

blocks.alt: A Genuine Leakage Trap Specific to Date Features
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443135308-968605892.png

Days since last purchase is genuinely safe, it is knowable at the exact moment a real prediction needs to be made, since the last purchase has already happened by then. Days until next purchase is genuinely not safe at all, it requires knowing something that has not happened yet, a direct, specific instance of the temporal leakage covered in the Data Leakage topic earlier in this course.

This distinction is genuinely easy to get wrong when engineering date features quickly, always ask, for every date derived feature, whether it would genuinely be computable using only information available up to the real moment of prediction, not information that depends on what happens afterward.

This topic pushed the basic date extraction from earlier in this module considerably further, cyclical encoding, recency features, domain informed holiday flags, and time of day extraction, while flagging a genuine, specific leakage risk unique to this kind of feature. Together, these techniques genuinely mine a single date column for far more signal than the basic day of week and month extraction alone.

The next topic, Text Features, applies this same deepen the basics approach to the other major unstructured form first covered briefly in Feature Extraction, going considerably further into free form text than word count and sentiment score alone.

items: Raw month or day numbers make temporally adjacent values, like December and January, look numerically far apart.
Cyclical sine and cosine encoding wraps date parts into a circle, fixing that numerical distance problem.
Days since a reference event, like last purchase, is a genuinely powerful, broadly useful recency feature.
Holiday flags combine domain knowledge with date extraction, connecting directly back to the Domain Features topic.
A full date and time value also yields hour and is business hours as additional useful features.
A feature like days until next purchase is genuine temporal leakage; only use information knowable at prediction time.
